column3: rationale
The arm64 port establishes its address constants while topic 0015 selects and sizes the common scalable Darwin native-address profile.
The arm64 port owns mmap policy while topic 0015 rejects guest mappings that cross the shared sparse native hole.
The arm64 port owns its relax primitive while the fixed-carrier topic adds a safe cooperative IPI boundary.
The arm64 signal port owns its restorer while topic 0015 moves the trampoline with the selected guest task ceiling.
The shared architecture topic establishes Darwin-capable UML configuration while topic 0023 advertises suspend after adding the SMP CPU-hotplug implementation used by the generic PM core.
The device topic introduces Darwin networking while topic 0021 moves receive processing onto budgeted NAPI polling.
The device topic adapts UBD host I/O, while topic 0024 lets direct images batch discard ranges without changing upstream COW handling.

Darwin vhost-user transport support remains in topic 0010, the generic 64-bit DMA-mask correction stays independently droppable as topic 0014, and topic 0027 adds the negotiated standard shared-region transport used by host-visible Virtio-GPU blobs.
The device topic owns Darwin input while topic 0020 exposes the display-mapped pointer as a direct touchscreen.
The shared task-layout contract remains in topic 0001 while topic 0015 selects the scalable Darwin guest unmapped base.
The shared contract owns the TLB flush interface while topic 0030 routes the kernel range through a sync whose result cannot be discarded.
The shared contract owns kernel-side host helpers, topic 0019 adds cooperative progress checkpoints, and topic 0023 adds the suspend-entry acknowledgement hook.
The shared host contract remains in topic 0001, topic 0018 adds local IPI raise, topic 0022 adds physical-range reclamation, and topic 0026 adds the virtual CPU's model name.
The reclamation topic owns Darwin physical-range reporting while topic 0027 adds the guarded shared-memory aperture and its constant-time physical lookup.
The execution core owns Linux task entry while topic 0016 adapts activation to fixed Darwin vCPU carriers.
The MMU bootstrap owns CPU0 setup while topic 0016 installs the Darwin signal stack on its carrier.

The MMU topic owns synchronized user access, topic 0019 adds safe cooperative progress boundaries, and topic 0029 answers mmap-lock contention in a pagefault-disabled walk with an RCU page-table walk instead of a fault.
The SMP core owns IPI dispatch while topic 0018 adds the irq-work vector and local raise.
The timer core owns Darwin delivery while topic 0019 exposes safe cooperative progress checkpoints.

The MMU topic owns Darwin invalidation, topic 0019 adds a quiescent progress boundary after it completes, and topic 0030 makes a kernel-range sync complete or stop the kernel instead of returning a discarded error.
The MMU core owns guest fault dispatch while topic 0015 rejects faults that intersect the shared sparse native hole.

The execution core owns task-size setup, topic 0015 selects and sizes the common Apple address window, topic 0023 acknowledges host-controlled suspend at the platform entry boundary, topic 0026 reports the emulator's CPU model name, and topic 0027 reserves the bounded guarded shared-memory GPA aperture inside that native layout.

The Darwin host topic owns private services, topic 0016 replaces per-task scheduler hooks and adds carrier stop handling, and topic 0028 declares the virtual-CPU ownership query a synchronous host fault is qualified against.
The Darwin host topic owns entry while topic 0016 keeps last-ditch stop handling on fixed carriers.
The Darwin host topic owns physical-memory setup while topic 0022 selects anonymous backing and range reclamation.
The Darwin host topic owns host process services and installs the process-wide fault handlers, while topic 0028 claims the boot thread as their owner before those handlers exist.

The Darwin host topic owns logical IRQ state, topic 0016 pins it to fixed vCPU carriers, and topic 0028 admits a synchronous host fault into the guest path only from the thread which owns the virtual CPU it would be attributed to.

The Darwin host topic owns fault dispatch, topic 0015 validates sparse guest ranges, topic 0016 supplies fixed-carrier scheduling and stop boundaries, and topic 0026 advances the asserted bridge ABI identity.

The Darwin host topic owns SMP transport, topic 0016 supplies fixed carriers, topic 0018 raises irq work locally, topic 0019 adds cooperative progress service, and topic 0028 reports which virtual CPU, if any, the running host thread carries.
The Darwin host service implementation owns host start-up probing while topic 0026 forwards the emulator's CPU model name.
The Darwin host topic owns idle waits while topic 0016 adds the fixed-carrier stop descriptor.
The Darwin bridge owns ABI declarations, topic 0015 carries the signal-restorer address, topic 0016 adds the active-stop event, and topic 0026 advances the identity for the CPU model name.
The Darwin bridge owns ABI identity while topics 0015, 0016 and 0026 advance the address, carrier-stop and CPU-identity contracts.
The Darwin bridge owns the CPU entry points while topic 0026 adds the model-name query.
The Darwin bridge owns host declarations while topic 0016 exposes the per-run stop descriptor and predicate.
The Linux host topic owns SMP transport while topic 0018 adds the local irq-work raise.
